lessons.symptom: An expensive artifact-specific workflow runs for unrelated changes because its trigger watches a broad directory instead of the files and runtime it actually owns.
lessons.rootCause: Workflow trigger scope evolved independently from the workflow's consumed files and artifact ownership, so a convenient broad glob became an unnecessary deploy and browser-test fan-out.
lessons.failedApproach: Keep broad directory triggers such as tools/** for convenience even when the workflow reads or executes only a small owned subset.
lessons.requiredAction: Inventory the files the workflow actually reads, executes or validates; scope pull-request triggers to those owned paths plus the workflow/config paths required for self-canary, while preserving all substantive runtime assertions.
lessons.prevention: Expensive deploy, browser and artifact-specific workflows must trigger only from semantically owned or consumed paths; unrelated changes must not invoke them.
lessons.evidenceRule: A proven scope fix requires both sides: an unrelated Brain-only tool change creates no artifact-specific preview run, while a direct owned V18 tool or workflow change still triggers and passes the exact-head canary.
